text.audienceNote: VP and C-suite clicks on healthcare LinkedIn ads rose to 26 in October from 6 in September, the most this year, and real estate, finance and strategy leaders clicked 79 times, up from 15. Real estate, facilities and finance titles grew to 12% of impressions from 9%, and 81% of impressions reached directors and above. The next step is growing reach with real estate, facilities and finance leaders.
text.searchTermsNote: Broad terms such as "healthcare solution providers" (82 clicks, $130) and "healthcare management companies" (29 clicks, $62) took the most clicks in September and October. Negative keywords for software, management and listing searches would keep spend on real estate intent.
text.budgetNote: Conferences ($52K) and videography ($20K) are budgeted in November and December, so year-end utilization depends on those landing.
text.fatigueNote: No sign of fatigue: the Outlook ad has run 10 months and its click-through rate went from 1.66% in its first two months to 1.72% in the last two, and Boldt Difference rose from 0.79% to 1.64%. Refresh on frequency (more than about 4 impressions per person per month) rather than on a calendar.
bestPractices: Lead with a point of view on cost and risk
Cost-certainty statements ("The lowest number rarely survives delivery.") average 1.86% click-through vs 1.05% for brand promises and 0.54% for direct asks.
Keep Boldt out of the headline
Headlines that name Boldt average 0.87% vs 1.54% without; the logo and page name already carry the brand.
Complete-sentence headlines average 1.65% vs 1.05% for 6 words or fewer, and cost about a quarter as much per conversion ($188 vs $807).
Earn the click before asking for a meeting
"Schedule a meeting" and "Contact our experts" average 0.54% at $9.98 per click. Save direct asks for retargeting.
Match every high-click ad with a converting page
Cost-certainty ads drew 1,028 clicks and 4 conversions; give the landing page a clear next step before adding budget.
Use document ads for retargeting only
Document lead gen costs $1,261 per conversion vs $330 for image ads, with a 0.25% click-through rate.
Financing and ownership headlines average 0.74% at $6.93 per click. State the outcome (for example, capital freed or rent avoided) rather than the product name.
Test in pairs, judge at 10,000 impressions
Run 2 to 3 headlines per theme and wait for 10,000 impressions each before calling a winner.

exec.headline: October MQLs rose to 27 from 22 in September, and cost per MQL fell to $359 from $404. Our healthcare LinkedIn ads drew 26 VP and C-suite clicks, the most this year, at a cost per click of $1.36.

sections.title: Results
sections.body: Healthcare marketing produced 27 new MQLs in October, up from 22 in September but below 37 in October 2025, against a monthly goal of 37. Year to date, MQLs total 260, which is 70% of the conservative goal and 17% below the same months of 2025. SQLs remain ahead of last year at 33 through September versus 21 in 2025, and MQL-to-SQL conversion through September is 14.2% compared with 6.8% last year.

sections.title: What went well
bullets: More leads at a lower cost. MQLs rose 23% from September to 27, and cost per MQL fell to $359 from $404 on $9,687 of healthcare marketing spend.
LinkedIn got more efficient: cost per click fell to $1.36 from $4.15, click-through rate rose to 1.81% from 1.57%, conversions rose to 16 from 11, and LinkedIn visits to the site rose 16% to 123.

Our LinkedIn ads are reaching decision makers: VP and C-suite clicks reached 26 (up from 6), real estate, finance and strategy leaders clicked 79 times (up from 15), and real estate, facilities and finance titles grew to 12% of impressions from 9%.

159 HubSpot companies visited the site in October, up from 151, and 44 companies reached by our healthcare LinkedIn ads in October went on to visit the site, including Houston Methodist, Northwell Health and OhioHealth.

By our engagement definition, 54 healthcare companies engaged with Boldt for the first time in 12 months in October, and 570 companies have engaged so far in 2026. 10 of our 14 SQL companies this year had a call, meeting or 1:1 email with Boldt before becoming an SQL.

sections.title: Where we are focused
bullets: MQL volume trails last year: 260 from January through October versus 314 in 2025, down 17%. That holds cost per MQL at $449 for the year versus $390 in 2025.
Putting the LinkedIn budget back to work: healthcare LinkedIn spent $1,014 of $5,833 in October, so there is room to grow reach with real estate, facilities and finance leaders.
Google healthcare clicks dipped 10% to 3,190 and Google Ads visits fell 8% to 1,097, so we are tightening search terms to real estate intent.

sections.title: Budget
sections.body: Healthcare and shared marketing spend is $141K through October, 70% of the budget to date. October came in at $12.3K against $17.4K budgeted; LinkedIn healthcare spent $1,014 of its $5,833 line and Google healthcare $1,448 of $2,441. Conferences ($52K) and videography ($20K) are scheduled for November and December.

nextMonth: Shift more LinkedIn budget toward real estate, facilities and finance leaders to build on October's gains.
Restart the cost-certainty image ads alongside the Outlook ads to use the unspent LinkedIn budget.
Relaunch the cost-certainty landing page with a shorter form and a clearer next step.
Tighten Google search terms to real estate intent.
Mirror the best Google healthcare keywords in Bing, which brought 122 visits in October.

qbr.headline: Healthcare website sessions tripled in Q3, to 4,114 from 1,336 in Q2, on about the same ad spend ($16.9K vs $17.2K). Google clicks doubled at the same $0.37 per click after the tiered healthcare campaigns launched, and LinkedIn drew more clicks on less spend.
qbr.takeaway: Ad spend held flat while healthcare traffic tripled, so cost per website session fell from $12.89 to $4.10. Leads did not keep pace: MQLs were 77 vs 81 in Q2 and SQLs were 5 vs 13. The next gains come from turning the larger audience into conversations: a landing page matched to each Google ad group, retargeting for companies that saw LinkedIn ads, and more mid-funnel offers.

recs.title: Match a landing page to each Google ad group
recs.why: Q3 cost per click ranged from $0.28 (Competitor) to $0.56 (Healthcare Development Core), and Core, Medical Real Estate and Healthcare RE Firms & Services each drew between 1,407 and 2,027 clicks. Each theme is a different search intent.
recs.action: Build one page per ad group theme with a headline that repeats the keyword theme and one clear next step. Better landing page relevance lifts Quality Score, which lowers cost per click. Judge it on conversion rate and cost per click by ad group.

recs.title: Retarget companies that saw LinkedIn ads
recs.why: In October, 968 companies saw healthcare LinkedIn ads and 44 visited the site. Of 311 healthcare companies active on LinkedIn, 75 later came back through a Google ad, about 11 days later on average.
recs.action: Add a retargeting audience of companies that engaged with or saw the ads, and serve them the Outlook and project case studies. Keep the awareness campaigns running so the retargeting pool keeps filling.

recs.title: Build more mid-funnel offers for LinkedIn lead generation
recs.why: LinkedIn conversions rose to 40 in Q3 from 19 in Q2 while LinkedIn spend fell 18%. The Outlook is still carrying most of the offer load.
recs.action: Add 2 to 3 offers to rotate: a project case study, a cost-certainty or feasibility checklist, and a short webinar or recorded briefing. Use them in lead gen forms and the retargeting audience.

expansion.title: Make Microsoft Ads (Bing) a standing channel
expansion.why: Bing brought 122 healthcare sessions in October, up from 14 in September, as the first keywords went live.
expansion.action: Once the Google healthcare tiers and negative keywords are mirrored there (see the November list), give Bing a set monthly budget and review it next to Google each month on cost per session and known companies visiting.

expansion.title: Lock a measurement baseline before the rebrand
expansion.why: A rebrand is the biggest measurement risk ahead. Q2 and Q3 give two clean quarters to compare against.
expansion.action: Record branded search clicks (4,158 on the Brand campaign in Q3), direct and other sessions (199 in Q3), known companies visiting (159 in October) and VP and C-suite clicks before anything changes publicly. Run old and new brand keywords side by side during the switch, and refresh creative on every channel at once.

expansion.title: Test Meta Ads for buying-committee reach
expansion.why: LinkedIn cost $6.28 per click in Q3 against $0.37 on Google. Meta can reach the same health system and finance contacts for less, as awareness rather than lead capture.
expansion.action: Upload HubSpot contacts and recent site visitors as custom audiences, promote the Outlook and case studies, and cap the budget. Judge it on return visits from known companies, not cost per lead.

expansion.title: Run a small ChatGPT Ads test
expansion.why: Buyers increasingly research in AI assistants before they search, and that first touch is not measured today.
expansion.action: Treat it as a capped learning test once targeting fits a B2B audience. Point ads at research content, run it for a full quarter, and measure known company visits rather than platform clicks.

qbr.note: Launch these in order rather than all at once. Ad spend is about $17K a quarter across two platforms, so splitting it four ways before Microsoft Ads proves out would leave every channel too small to read.

defMql.definition: A healthcare company in HubSpot that actively engaged in the past 12 months: a website visit, a LinkedIn, Google or Bing ad click, or an email click (marketing or 1:1). Counted by organization.
defMql.newRule: New = engaged in October with no engagement in the 12 months before.
defMql.window: LinkedIn clicks and email clicks are tracked back to November 2025. Website visits and Google ad clicks are counted from March 16, 2026, and Bing ad clicks from their September 2026 launch. For 1:1 emails HubSpot keeps the most recent click on each contact.
defMql.domainNote: Parent and child companies that share one website domain, such as a health system and its hospitals, can't always be told apart, so their activity may be combined. We're working through this with Factors.
defMql.ytdNote: Website visits are tracked from March 16, so January and February count LinkedIn and email engagement only.
defMql.listNote: LinkedIn reports clicks by company for each campaign, not for each ad within it. LinkedIn click dates come from Factors, which records LinkedIn activity every few days. Google and Bing clicks are website visits from those ads. Pages viewed and impressions come from Factors and cover May 9 to October 31. Website visits are counted by week, so the most recent date for a visit is the start of that week.

rows.src: Factors, average per day in October

dow.note: Google and Bing ad visits and email clicks by healthcare companies in HubSpot, January to October 2026, one per company per day. LinkedIn ad clicks and website visits are reported by month and week, so they aren't placed on a day.
dow.allNote: Share of each source's activity by day, January to October 2026. LinkedIn and Google clicks and GA4 sessions are daily totals from each platform. LinkedIn click dates in the MQL calendar come from Factors, which loads LinkedIn company data every two to four days, so they bunch up on those load days; LinkedIn's own daily clicks peak on Monday and Tuesday.

loc.note: State from each company's HubSpot record. Health systems are listed at their headquarters state.
